subject: math
source: English National Curriculum — Mathematics programmes of study: key stage 2 (Year 6), DfE 2013; KS2 mathematics test framework (STA)

objectives: Read, write, order and compare numbers up to 10,000,000
Determine the value of each digit
Use place value to solve problems

weeks.topic: Rounding, negative numbers and number problems
objectives: Round any whole number to a required degree of accuracy
Use negative numbers in context and calculate intervals across zero
Solve number and practical problems

weeks.topic: Written and mental addition and subtraction
objectives: Add and subtract large numbers using formal methods
Perform mental calculations with mixed operations and large numbers
Solve multi-step problems choosing efficient methods
Multiply multi-digit numbers up to 4 digits by a 2-digit number
Estimate to check the reasonableness of answers
Apply long multiplication to word problems
Divide numbers up to 4 digits by a 2-digit number using long division
Interpret remainders as whole numbers, fractions or by rounding
Use short division where appropriate

weeks.topic: Common factors, common multiples and primes
objectives: Identify common factors, common multiples and prime numbers
Use prime factorisation to find factors
Solve problems using factors and multiples
Use knowledge of the order of operations to carry out calculations
Use brackets to change the order of a calculation
Spot and correct errors in calculations
Use common factors to simplify fractions
Use common multiples to express fractions in the same denomination
Compare and order fractions, including fractions > 1

weeks.topic: Adding and subtracting fractions with different denominators
objectives: Add and subtract fractions with different denominators
Add and subtract mixed numbers
Solve problems with fractions in context
Multiply simple pairs of proper fractions (e.g. 1/4 × 1/2 = 1/8)
Write the answer in its simplest form
Represent fraction multiplication with diagrams
Divide proper fractions by whole numbers (e.g. 1/3 ÷ 2 = 1/6)
Use diagrams to explain the division
Solve problems involving sharing fractions
Associate a fraction with division
Calculate decimal equivalents of fractions (e.g. 3/8 = 0.375)
Recall and use equivalences between fractions, decimals and percentages
Multiply and divide numbers by 10, 100 and 1,000 giving answers up to 3 decimal places
Multiply one-digit numbers with up to 2 decimal places by whole numbers
Use written division where answers have up to 2 decimal places
Convert between standard units of length, mass, volume and time using up to 3 decimal places
Convert between miles and kilometres
Solve problems involving measures

weeks.topic: Term 1 review: number, fractions and decimals
objectives: Revisit the four operations with formal methods
Consolidate fractions and decimals calculations
Practise arithmetic test-style questions
Solve problems involving the calculation of percentages (e.g. 15% of 360)
Use percentages for comparison
Find percentage increases and discounts in context
Solve problems involving the relative sizes of two quantities
Use ratio notation (a:b)
Find missing values using multiplication and division facts
Solve problems involving similar shapes where the scale factor is known or can be found
Solve problems involving unequal sharing and grouping
Use scale on maps and drawings

weeks.topic: Algebra: simple formulae and missing numbers
objectives: Use simple formulae
Express missing number problems algebraically
Substitute values into expressions

weeks.topic: Algebra: linear sequences and two unknowns
objectives: Generate and describe linear number sequences
Find pairs of numbers that satisfy an equation with two unknowns
Enumerate possibilities of combinations of two variables
Recognise when it is possible to use formulae for area
Calculate the area of parallelograms and triangles
Recognise that shapes with the same area can have different perimeters
Calculate, estimate and compare volume of cubes and cuboids using cm³ and m³
Use the formula length × width × height
Extend to other units such as mm³ and km³

weeks.topic: Angles in triangles, quadrilaterals and polygons
objectives: Find unknown angles in triangles, quadrilaterals and regular polygons
Recognise vertically opposite angles
Recognise angles where they meet at a point or on a straight line
Name parts of circles, including radius, diameter and circumference
Know that the diameter is twice the radius
Draw 2-D shapes and build 3-D shapes from nets

weeks.topic: Coordinates in four quadrants and transformations
objectives: Describe positions on the full coordinate grid (all four quadrants)
Draw and translate simple shapes on the coordinate plane
Reflect shapes in the axes

weeks.topic: Statistics: pie charts, line graphs and the mean
objectives: Interpret and construct pie charts and line graphs
Calculate and interpret the mean as an average
Solve problems using statistical data

weeks.topic: Mock assessment: arithmetic and reasoning papers
objectives: Complete an arithmetic paper under timed conditions
Complete two reasoning papers
Identify personal areas for revision
Practise efficient methods for all question types in the arithmetic paper
Check answers using inverse operations and estimation
Manage time across the paper

weeks.topic: SATs revision: number, fractions and percentages reasoning
objectives: Solve multi-step reasoning problems with number and fractions
Explain reasoning clearly in words
Show working for two-mark questions

weeks.topic: SATs revision: geometry and measures reasoning
objectives: Revisit angles, area, perimeter and volume problems
Apply unit conversions in context
Interpret shapes and coordinates questions

weeks.topic: SATs revision: ratio, algebra and statistics
objectives: Revisit ratio, scale factor and algebra questions
Interpret tables, graphs and pie charts
Practise full reasoning papers

weeks.topic: Financial maths: budgets, profit and loss
objectives: Plan a budget for a class event using decimals and percentages
Calculate profit and loss
Compare value for money
Explore number patterns and make conjectures
Use algebra to express a general rule
Test and justify generalisations

weeks.topic: Bridging to KS3: powers, negative numbers and algebraic notation
objectives: Calculate with negative numbers in all four operations
Use index notation for squares and cubes
Simplify simple algebraic expressions

weeks.topic: Geometry project: designing a scale model
objectives: Draw plans using a scale factor
Build a 3-D model from nets
Calculate surface area and volume of the model
Show fluency across the Year 6 programme
Apply reasoning to unfamiliar problems
Explain methods and check answers

weeks.topic: Year 6 review and transition to Year 7
objectives: Reflect on strengths and targets in mathematics
Consolidate key calculation methods
Prepare for KS3 mathematics
